newsitem.title: INDIA: India CRISIL gives "P1+" rating for Oil India Ltd.
newsitem.headline: India CRISIL gives "P1+" rating for Oil India Ltd.

text.p: India's Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) said on Wednesday it has assigned a "P1+" rating to the 500 million rupees short term debt programme of Oil India Ltd (OIL) indicating that the degree of safety regarding timely payment on the instrument is very strong.

It said in a statement OIL is primarily engaged in exploration and production of hydrocarbons (crude oil and natural gas), extraction of liquified petroleum gas (LPG) and transportation of crude oil and natural gas through its pipeline network.

OIL has been given a petroleum exploration licence to explore for the possibility of hydrocarbons in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Orissa offshore, Gujarat offshore and Uttar Pradesh (Ganga valley). However, at present OIL's operations are primarily restricted to the north eastern region of India. As at March 31, 1996 the total crude oil and natural gas reserves of OIL were 64.4 million MT and 90.8 billion cubic meters respectively.
Further, for the year 1995/96 the total production of crude oil was 2.88 million MT and the production of natural gas was 1.4 billion cubic meters, CRISIL said.

Out of the 26 sedimentary basis in India covering a total area of 1.72 million square KM, OIL is operating in around seven percent of this area and the remaining area (93 percent) has been allocated to Oil and Natural Gas Commission (ONGC) in line with this sharp difference in the operating areas the crude oil reserves and natural gas reserves of ONGC are considerable higher at 675.20 million MT and 560 billion cubic meters as compared to OIL's reserves.

The total prognosticated reserves in OIL's area of operations are estimated at 2 billion MT, out of which the company has been able to discover around 748.40 million MT. This leaves a large gap for further discovery. While OIL in the past has been exploring for hydrocarbons in regions other than Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, it has only been successful to a limited extent.

The statement also said that OIL is covered under the administered price mechanism (APM) which in the case of crude and natural gas guarantees a 15 percent post tax returns on the capital employed in oil exploration and a reimbursements of all operational expenses. On account of this guaranteed return the overall profitability of the company is high. On a operating income of 5,735.10 million rupees for the year 1995/96 the company earned a profit of 2,064.60 million rupees. The company had a low gearing (total debt/tangible networth) of 0.12 as at March 31, 1996 and the coverage (PBDIT/Interest and Finance Charges) was comfortable at 12.02 for the years 1995/96.
